followUp.question: Single phase or three phase?
followUp.hint: Single phase is the ordinary household meter and most of the 7.24 million unmetered customers. Three phase is for shops, factories and large buildings.

analysis.summary: A single-phase STS prepaid meter assembled in Lagos from an imported parts kit: built, calibrated, tested, certified and sealed here. Assembly, not making the circuit board from scratch.

materials.name: Circuit board
materials.role: The brain. Measures the electricity, remembers your credit, runs the software.
materials.source: Imported. Nobody in Nigeria makes these yet.

materials.name: Current sensor
materials.role: Measures how much electricity is flowing through.

materials.name: Relay
materials.role: The switch that cuts power when credit runs out and restores it on top-up.

materials.name: Screen and keypad
materials.role: Shows remaining units and tamper warnings; takes the 20-digit token.
materials.source: Screen imported. Keypad imported, or moulded here.

materials.name: Plastic casing
materials.role: Housing, back plate and terminal cover. Sealable and weatherproof.
materials.source: Can be made in Nigeria. Aba and Ogun have the moulding machines.

materials.name: Terminal block
materials.role: Where the wires from the wall connect.

materials.name: Backup battery
materials.role: Keeps the clock and tamper record running when power is off.

materials.name: Seals, label, manual
materials.role: Tamper seals, the NEMSA mark, user instructions.

materials.name: Security credentials
materials.role: The digital keys that make the DisCo's tokens work on this specific meter.
materials.source: Licensed through the STS Association, loaded in your own factory

process.title: Check the kits
process.detail: Count and inspect incoming boxes and test a sample of boards. A bad batch caught here costs nothing; caught after calibration it costs everything. Half a day a batch.

process.title: Prepare the casings
process.detail: Check, clean and label the plastic housings.

process.title: Build it
process.detail: Seat the board in the casing, connect relay and sensor, fit keypad and screen. Anti-static benches, because boards die from a static shock. About 4 minutes a meter.

process.title: Load software and keys
process.detail: Flash the software, then inject the security credentials from a locked device. This makes the DisCo's tokens work on your meter. 1 minute a meter.

process.title: Calibrate
process.detail: Check each meter against a known-accurate reference at several power levels and adjust until it reads correctly. The slow step that sets the line's pace.

process.title: Safety test
process.detail: Apply high voltage to prove the insulation holds. NEMSA requires it. 1 minute a meter.

process.title: Burn-in
process.detail: Run meters powered on a rack for 4 to 8 hours to catch early failures before they reach a customer's wall.

process.title: Seal and mark
process.detail: Fit tamper seals, laser-mark the serial number and register it with the DisCo.

process.title: Pack
process.detail: Box with manual and warranty card, stack on pallets.

context: Of about 13.3 million registered electricity customers, roughly 6 million have meters. The other 7.24 million are on estimated billing.
Three pots of money are live: ₦100bn under the Presidential Meter Initiative, ₦28bn under Tranche B of the Meter Acquisition Fund, and DISREP on a $500 million World Bank facility.
The rules already say 30% of contracted meter volumes must come from local firms.
A Meter Asset Provider must hold at least 2,000 meters in stock to bid for work, so 2,000 is the smallest batch that gets you into the market.
This is assembly: the circuit board comes from abroad, as it does for almost every meter assembled outside China. The plastic casing is the first part worth bringing fully in-house.
A 300 meter a day line costs $45,000 to $90,000, roughly ₦95m landed and installed. No circuit board machinery is needed to start.

cost.verdict: Assembling here is 36% cheaper: ₦19,100 a meter, or ₦38.2m on a batch of 2,000, and it holds all year. Meters sell for ₦133,300 to ₦150,500 on the Ikeja approved list, so the margin over your ₦33,300 cost is about ₦100,000. But the advantage rests on the 35% levy on finished imports: without it the saving falls to about ₦8,600. The line costs about ₦95m and the first saleable batch is about 20 weeks away, mostly waiting on approvals.
caveats: The 35% levy is the whole margin. It was suspended for a year in 2020 to speed a three million meter rollout. Remove it and your saving drops from ₦19,100 to about ₦8,600.
Government keeps buying from China: a 2024 deal sent 1,437,500 smart meters to Chinese firms, and a $340,000 bid deposit on an earlier tender priced local makers out.
About 2.5 million meters have been delivered and only about 150,000 installed. Installers say the ₦3,000 fee isn't worth the trip. The shortage has moved from making meters to fitting them.
The rules punish going deeper: kit assemblers pay 5% duty with no VAT, while a full manufacturer pays duty on every component. Assemble first; mould the casing here, not the electronics.
NEMSA, NERC, SON and STS fees are not published. Ask them in writing before you budget.
Kit and equipment prices are ranges, not quotes.

groups.name: Materials
groups.description: The kit comes from China. Casings, labels and security printing can come from Nigeria, and the casing is the first part worth bringing in-house.

suppliers.name: Chinese meter kit suppliers
suppliers.note: Ask for kit pricing, not finished meters, and for the international test documentation up front. Kits ship out of Ningbo, Shenzhen or Wenzhou.

price.label: Parts kit
price.basis: About $15 a kit at ₦1,390/$, before freight and duty

suppliers.name: CountMe Chemicals
suppliers.note: Raw material for casings, not the finished casing.

suppliers.name: Nigerian injection moulders
suppliers.note: Nigeria has plenty of moulding machines sitting underused. Casings are bulky to ship and cheap to mould.

suppliers.name: iPrints Nigeria
suppliers.note: Labels for seals and the NEMSA mark.

suppliers.name: Cardstel Solutions
suppliers.note: Security printing and holograms for seals and packaging.

groups.name: Workshops
groups.description: The established meter makers: your competition, and a guide to where a newcomer fits.

suppliers.name: MOJEC International
suppliers.note: The largest, with over 1.5 million meters deployed. You won't beat it on volume and shouldn't try.

suppliers.name: MEMMCOL (Momas)
suppliers.note: The loudest voice on tariff policy; its chairman has warned about suspending the levy on finished meters.

groups.name: Services
groups.description: Approvals first, then clearing, then the buyers. Five approvals run longer than the factory build.

suppliers.name: NEMSA
suppliers.note: No meter can legally be fitted without type approval. Talk to them while still choosing a platform. Fee not published.

suppliers.name: NERC
suppliers.note: Licenses you to assemble meters, and separately to sell and install directly. Fees not published.

suppliers.name: SON
suppliers.note: Product standard mark for goods made in Nigeria.

suppliers.name: STS Association
suppliers.note: Your own identity in the token system so tokens from any DisCo work on your meters. Recurring fees. Sort it before ordering the key station.

suppliers.name: Advance Logistics Services
suppliers.note: 77a Shipeolu Street. Ask whether they have cleared meter kits before: the 5% assembler duty depends on correct paperwork.

suppliers.name: Alov Air-Sea
suppliers.note: 5 Adegoke Estate. Pick an agent before placing the order, not after the container lands.

suppliers.name: AGL (formerly Bolloré)
suppliers.note: Larger and more expensive, but unlikely to leave your container sitting and running up demurrage.

suppliers.name: DisCos and MAP vendors
suppliers.note: Each MAP vendor must hold 2,000 meters to bid, and the big makers won't take an order that small. That is your opening.

suppliers.name: EMMAN and MMAAN
suppliers.note: Tariff policy moves through these groups. Join one or you'll hear about changes after they've cost you.

steps.title: Choose a platform and kit partner
steps.detail: Pick a meter platform and a Chinese kit supplier. Get the IEC 62055-31 and IEC 62053-21 test documentation up front, because NEMSA will ask for it.

steps.title: Approvals
steps.detail: NEMSA type approval, NERC certification and the STS licence. Start on day one: this is the long pole and nothing ships without it.

steps.title: Equipment
steps.detail: Order the calibration bench and key station, clear them at the port, install and commission. Everything else on the list is quick.

steps.title: Hire and train
steps.detail: Operators need a week. The technicians and supervisor need longer and should be in place before the machines arrive.

steps.title: Trial build
steps.detail: Expect the first hundred meters to fail something. Far better here than in the official test.

steps.title: First saleable batch
steps.detail: Build 2,000 meters in about 7 working days: 300 a day, paced by calibration. Add bench positions to go faster.
